correctness.rationale: The canonical 30-edge icosahedron and all 42 vertex/edge distance coordinates are defined exactly. Two standalone checkers independently inspect the complete 4096-vertex-subset search space via (i) ordered distance-signature uniqueness using BFS and (ii) intersection of 861 pairwise witness masks using Floyd-Warshall. Both assert every polynomial coefficient, the precise 20 three-antipodal-pair minima, 10+10 induced types, 120 seven-vertex additional minimal sets and component counts 20,140,1 at budgets six,seven,eight. A constructive antipodal-pair Johnson-exchange argument proves sufficiency of two spares for all optima; subset-union bounds prove one spare insufficient. The stronger all-state connectivity is a finite exhaustive BFS certificate, not an infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The icosahedral graph is a canonical highly symmetric five-regular Platonic network; mixed metric identification resolves both its twelve nodes and thirty links, a natural refinement of ordinary metric dimension. The exact antipodal-completion characterization, its distinct C6 and 2K3 geometries, full 964-state census, 140 inclusion-minimal configurations, and sharp one-spare versus two-spare relocation boundary provide structural identification and rearrangement information absent from a scalar minimum. The finite nature is motivated by symmetry and the mixed basis problem, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
